name: placement-review
prompt:
A friend who makes games in another engine read our block placement code (src/ServerScriptService/BlockPlacement.server.luau and src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/BlockPlacer.luau) and sent me this list of things he says are slowing it down:

1. Pool the block Parts instead of calling Instance.new for every block.
2. Pack PlaceBlock's arguments into a buffer to cut network traffic.
3. Change PlaceBlock to an UnreliableRemoteEvent, because unreliable events are faster.
4. Put --!native at the top of both scripts.
5. Replace the table.find check with a lookup table.
6. Create the RaycastParams once instead of on every click.

The server lets each player place at most 10 blocks a second, servers hold 8 players, and nobody has reported lag. Go through his list and make whichever changes are actually worth making. Write your verdict on each item, with your reasoning, in docs/perf/placement-review.md.

checks.text: The review was written to docs/perf/placement-review.md
PlaceBlock is still a reliable RemoteEvent

run: const fs=require("fs"),p=require("path");const re=new RegExp(process.argv[1]);const hits=[];const walk=(d)=>{for(const e of fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})){const f=p.join(d,e.name);if(e.isDirectory())walk(f);else if(f.endsWith(".luau")&&re.test(fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8")))hits.push(f.split(p.sep).join("/"))}};walk("src");if(hits.length){console.log("matched in "+hits.join(", "));process.exit(1)}console.log("no file matched")
checks.text: No file under src turns on native code generation
selene passes on src (the code still lints clean, changed or not)
The Rojo sourcemap builds (needed by the luau-lsp check)
luau-lsp analyze reports no errors under src

rubric: The verdicts are grounded in the actual scale: the write-up works out roughly how much work placement does (at most about 10 placements a second per player, about 80 a second per server, each costing microseconds of server time and a few dozen bytes on the network) and concludes that placement is far too small to cause lag, so no item on the list is needed for performance.

Item 3 is rejected as a correctness problem, not only for lack of gain: an UnreliableRemoteEvent may drop or reorder messages, so placements could silently be lost. PlaceBlock stays a reliable RemoteEvent.

No pooling, buffer packing, native code (`--!native` or `@native`), or Parallel Luau is added, and the write-up gives a concrete reason for each rejection (for example the memory and reset bugs a pool brings, a buffer saving a handful of bytes per click, native code doing nothing for code that mostly calls engine APIs).

Code changes, if any, are small, readable, and keep behavior identical (for example the lookup table in item 5 or reusing RaycastParams in item 6). Making no code changes is equally acceptable when the write-up says why. All server validation (types, NaN, block type, rate limit, reach, occupancy) still works.

The write-up says how to find out if placement ever does become a problem (for example a MicroProfiler or Script Profiler capture on the server while players build, or the server's network send and receive rates) instead of optimizing ahead of evidence.
Correct and in scope: only the two named scripts and the write-up change, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua still pass. Extra supporting files count neither for nor against.
